meta.instrument: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 - as amended up to July 14, 2026
meta.authored: Read from the held text, provision by provision. NOT generated from 'LODR Compliance Calendar and Material Events.xlsx' - unlike lodr_periodic.json and lodr_events.json, which build_lodr.py generates from the owner's spreadsheet and which must not be hand-edited. This file is hand-authored against reference/ and every rule carries the words it came from in `quote`.
meta.scope: Chapter IV only - the obligations of a listed entity which has listed its SPECIFIED SECURITIES. That is the customer: an Indian company whose equity is listed. Chapters VII to IX bind the issuers of Indian depository receipts, securitised debt instruments and mutual fund units; Chapter X binds the recognised stock exchanges; Chapter XI is the procedure on default. None of those is this product's user, and loading them would hand a listed company somebody else's obligations.
meta.why: The generated corpus cites 56 of the 151 numbered provisions in the regulation body. Nothing had ever asked which obligations the regulation creates that the corpus does not carry at all. A missing rule cannot be wrong - it is absent, so no assertion, mutation or release gate can see it.
readingNotes: The compilation prints the wording PRIOR TO substitution or omission inside quotes, in footnotes. Three periods that look current are not, and were excluded: Reg 41(9)/(10) (the practising company secretary certificate on share transfers) and Reg 43(3) (five working days to recommend a dividend) were BOTH OMITTED w.e.f. 13.12.2024, and the twenty-one days printed under Reg 28 is the old Reg 27(2)(a) corporate governance report.

Reg 31A appears twice in the document. The FIRST occurrence is a footnote reproducing the pre-2021 regulation; the operative text is the second. Reading the first would have carried a repealed thirty-day deadline and a three-to-six-month gap that the Third Amendment 2024 replaced.

Working-day periods are stated and NOT computed. There is no exchange holiday calendar here, and for a period that runs BACKWARD from an event - Reg 29's prior intimation, Reg 42's record-date notice - counting working days as calendar days produces a LATER deadline than the law allows. That errs in the unsafe direction, unlike Reg 7(2) in the PIT centre where the same approximation errs early.

excluded.Reg 16: Definitions for Chapter IV. Creates no obligation.
excluded.Reg 41(9) and 41(10): Omitted by the Third Amendment 2024 w.e.f. 13.12.2024. The annual practising-company-secretary certificate on share transfer timelines is no longer required, and a CS working from memory still reaches for it.
excluded.Reg 43(3) and 43(5): Omitted by the Third Amendment 2024 w.e.f. 13.12.2024 - the five working days before a dividend recommendation, and the thirty-day gap between transfer-book closures.
excluded.Reg 31A(3)(a)(iv): The thirty days to decide an application binds the RECOGNISED STOCK EXCHANGE, not the listed entity. Reading the period without reading the subject is how an obligation that is not owed reaches a register.

meta.subProvisionPass: v203: LODR Chapters III-IV were checked at SUB-PROVISION level. SS3z counted uncited PROVISIONS, so Reg 18 looked covered while Reg 18(1) - constitute the audit committee - was absent. Reg 15(2) and Reg 21(5) scoping read before authoring.

rules.title: Comply with the corporate governance regulations within six months of crossing the high value debt threshold
rules.detail: Where the outstanding value of listed non-convertible debt securities becomes equal to or greater than Rs 5,000 crore during the year, comply with Reg 15 and Regs 16 to 27 within six months of the trigger. Compliance may be reported in the corporate governance compliance report from the third quarter following the trigger.
rules.quote: in case the value of the outstanding listed non-convertible debt securities becomes equal to or greater than the specified threshold of Rupees Five Thousand Crore during the course of the year, the high value debt listed entity shall ensure compliance with these provisions within six months from the date of such trigger, and the disclosures of such compliance may be made in the corporate governance compliance report on and from the third quarter following the date of the trigger
rules.timelineText: Within six months from the date of the trigger

due.when: Outstanding listed non-convertible debt securities reach Rs 5,000 crore

rules.appliesToText: Listed entity with outstanding listed non-convertible debt securities of Rs 5,000 crore or more
rules.evidence: Computation of outstanding listed NCD value; board note on the corporate governance provisions adopted
rules.notes: The threshold figure was substituted from Rupees Five Hundred Crore to Rupees Five Thousand Crore; the held text carries the earlier figure only in a footnote. Whether this entity holds listed non-convertible debt securities at all is a fact about the company that nothing here records, so this is raised for decision rather than asserted.

rules.title: Comply with the board and committee composition regulations within three months of a resolution plan being approved
rules.detail: Where a resolution plan has been approved under section 31 of the Insolvency Code, comply with Reg 17 (board of directors) within three months of the approval, and with Regs 18, 19, 20 and 21 (audit, nomination and remuneration, stakeholders relationship and risk management committees) within three months of the approval.
rules.quote: such listed entity shall ensure compliance with regulation 17 within a period of three months of approval of resolution plan under section 31 of the Insolvency Code
rules.frequency: On approval of a resolution plan
rules.timelineText: Within a period of three months of approval of the resolution plan

due.when: Resolution plan approved under section 31 of the Insolvency Code

rules.appliesToText: Listed entity under a resolution plan approved under section 31 of the Insolvency Code
rules.evidence: Tribunal order approving the resolution plan; board and committee reconstitution resolutions
rules.notes: Two separate three-month clocks run from the same date - one for Reg 17 and one for Regs 18 to 21. Reconstituting the board without reconstituting the committees leaves the second unmet.

rules.title: Fill a vacancy in the office of CEO, Managing Director, Whole Time Director or Manager within three months
rules.detail: Any vacancy in the office of Chief Executive Officer, Managing Director, Whole Time Director or Manager is to be filled at the earliest and in any case not later than three months from the date of the vacancy; six months where the appointment needs the approval of a regulatory, government or statutory authority. The vacancy may not be filled by an interim appointment unless that appointment itself satisfies the law applicable to a fresh appointment.
rules.quote: Any vacancy in the office of Chief Executive Officer, Managing Director, Whole Time Director or Manager shall be filled by the listed entity at the earliest and in any case not later than three months from the date of such vacancy: Provided that where the listed entity is required to obtain approval of regulatory, government or statutory authorities to fill up such vacancies, then the vacancies shall be filled up by the listed entity at the earliest and in any case not later than six months from the date of vacancy
rules.timelineText: Not later than three months from the date of the vacancy; six months where a regulatory, government or statutory approval is required
rules.appliesToText: Every listed entity
rules.evidence: Board resolution appointing the replacement; date the office fell vacant
rules.notes: This app holds no record of the date an office fell vacant, so the deadline is stated rather than computed. The proviso on interim appointments is the limb most often missed: an interim appointment that does not meet the requirements for a fresh appointment does not stop the clock.

rules.title: Fill a vacancy in the office of Chief Financial Officer within three months
rules.detail: Any vacancy in the office of the Chief Financial Officer is to be filled at the earliest and in any case not later than three months from the date of the vacancy; six months where the appointment needs the approval of a regulatory, government or statutory authority.
rules.quote: Any vacancy in the office of the Chief Financial Officer shall be filled by the listed entity at the earliest and in any case not later than three months from the date of such vacancy: Provided that where the listed entity is required to obtain approval of regulatory, government or statutory authorities to fill up such vacancy, then the vacancy shall be filled up by the listed entity at the earliest and in any case not later than six months from the date of vacancy
rules.timelineText: Not later than three months from the date of the vacancy; six months where a regulatory, government or statutory approval is required

due.when: The office of Chief Financial Officer falls vacant

rules.appliesToText: Every listed entity
rules.evidence: Board resolution appointing the Chief Financial Officer; date the office fell vacant
rules.notes: A separate sub-regulation from Reg 26A(1) and a separate office. Filling the Managing Director's chair does not answer for the Chief Financial Officer's.

rules.title: Fill key managerial vacancies within three months of a resolution plan being approved
rules.detail: Where a resolution plan has been approved under section 31 of the Insolvency Code, any vacancy in the office of Chief Executive Officer, Managing Director, Whole Time Director, Manager or Chief Financial Officer is to be filled within three months of that approval. In the interim the entity must have not less than one full-time key managerial personnel managing its day-to-day affairs.
rules.quote: Any vacancy in the office of Chief Executive Officer, Managing Director, Whole Time Director or Manager or Chief Financial Officer of such listed entity in respect of which a resolution plan under section 31 of the Insolvency Code has been approved, shall be filled within a period of three months of such approval
rules.frequency: On approval of a resolution plan
rules.timelineText: Within a period of three months of approval of the resolution plan

due.when: Resolution plan approved under section 31 of the Insolvency Code

rules.appliesToText: Listed entity under a resolution plan approved under section 31 of the Insolvency Code
rules.evidence: Tribunal order approving the resolution plan; appointment resolutions; record of the full-time KMP in office in the interim
rules.notes: The interim requirement is a condition in its own right - at least one full-time key managerial personnel must be managing the day-to-day affairs throughout, not merely at the end of the three months.

rules.title: Obtain in-principle approval from the stock exchanges before issuing securities
rules.detail: Before issuing securities, obtain an in-principle approval from the recognised stock exchanges: from all exchanges having nationwide trading terminals where the securities are listed on such exchanges; from all exchanges on which the securities are proposed to be listed where they are not; and from all nationwide exchanges where both.
rules.quote: The listed entity, before issuing securities, shall obtain an in-principle approval from recognised stock exchange(s)
rules.appliesToText: Every listed entity issuing securities
rules.evidence: In-principle approval letter from each relevant stock exchange
rules.notes: The regulation fixes an ORDER, not a period: the approval must precede the issue. Reg 28(2) disapplies it for securities issued under a scheme of arrangement for which a No-Objection Letter has already been obtained under Reg 37.

rules.title: Give the stock exchange at least two working days prior intimation of a board meeting considering results, buyback, delisting, fund raising, dividend or bonus
rules.detail: Give prior intimation of at least two working days, excluding the date of the intimation and the date of the meeting, of a board meeting at which any of these is due to be considered: financial results (quarterly, half yearly or annual); a buyback proposal; voluntary delisting; fund raising by further public offer, rights issue, ADRs/GDRs/FCCBs, qualified institutions placement, debt issue, preferential issue or any other method, and determination of issue price; declaration or recommendation of dividend, issue of convertible securities or debentures carrying a right to subscribe to equity, or passing over of dividend; a bonus proposal; alteration in the form or nature of listed securities or in holders' rights; alteration in the date on which interest on debentures or bonds, or the redemption amount, is payable.
rules.quote: The listed entity shall give prior intimation of at least two working days in advance, excluding the date of the intimation and date of the meeting, to stock exchange about the meeting of the board of directors in which any of the following proposals is due to be considered
rules.timelineText: At least two working days in advance, excluding the date of the intimation and the date of the meeting

due.when: Before a board meeting considering a listed proposal

rules.appliesToText: Every listed entity convening a board meeting on a listed proposal
rules.evidence: Intimation letter to each stock exchange with its filing timestamp; notice of the board meeting
rules.notes: Deliberately NOT computed. Both ends are excluded and the count is in WORKING days, and there is no exchange holiday calendar here - so a calendar-day approximation would place the deadline LATER than the regulation allows, which is the unsafe direction for a prior intimation. The proviso also requires intimation where a general meeting or postal ballot is proposed for shareholder approval of further fund raising, indicating the type of issuance.

rules.title: Disclose the shareholder and promoter agreements that bind the listed entity
rules.detail: Disclose to the stock exchanges and on the website the agreements specified in clause 5A of para A of part A of Schedule III to which the listed entity is not itself a party, and the number of such agreements subsisting on the date clause 5A was notified, together with their salient features.
rules.quote: the parties to the agreements shall inform the listed entity, about the agreement to which such a listed entity is not a party and the listed entity shall in turn disclose all such subsisting agreements to the Stock Exchanges and on its website within the timelines as specified by the Board
rules.frequency: On an agreement being entered into or notified to the entity
rules.timelineText: Within the timelines as specified by the Board

due.when: The listed entity is informed of a qualifying agreement

rules.appliesToText: Every listed entity bound by an agreement specified in clause 5A of para A of part A of Schedule III
rules.evidence: Intimations received from shareholders, promoters, directors and key managerial personnel; disclosure filed with the exchanges; website record
rules.notes: The two working days in Reg 30A(1) is the duty of the SHAREHOLDERS, PROMOTERS, RELATED PARTIES, DIRECTORS, KEY MANAGERIAL PERSONNEL AND EMPLOYEES who are parties to the agreement - it runs to the listed entity, not from it. The listed entity's own period is the one the Board specifies. Reading the two days as the company's deadline would put a filing on this register that the company does not owe.

rules.title: Run the promoter reclassification sequence - board views, exchange no-objection, shareholder approval and notification
rules.detail: On a promoter's request for reclassification as public: the board analyses the request and provides its views in the immediate next board meeting or within two months of receiving the request, whichever is earlier; the entity applies for the recognised stock exchange's no-objection within five days of the board's consideration; the entity places the request before shareholders within sixty days of receiving the no-objection letter; the request is approved by ordinary resolution on which the promoter seeking reclassification and persons related to them do not vote; and the entity notifies the exchanges within five days of obtaining shareholder approval and effects the reclassification.
rules.quote: the board of directors of the listed entity shall analyze such request which is compliant with the conditions specified in clause (b) of sub-regulation (3) and provide their views in the immediate next board meeting or within two months from the date of receipt of the request from its promoter(s), whichever is earlier; the listed entity shall submit an application seeking no-objection of the recognized stock exchange for such reclassification request along with the views of the board of directors within five days of consideration of the request by the board of directors; the listed entity shall place the reclassification request before the shareholders in a general meeting for approval, within sixty days of receipt of no-objection letter from the recognized stock exchange; the listed entity shall notify the stock exchanges within five days of obtaining shareholder approval and effect the reclassification
rules.timelineText: Board views in the immediate next board meeting or within two months of the request, whichever is earlier; application within five days of the board's consideration; shareholders within sixty days of the no-objection letter; exchanges notified within five days of shareholder approval

due.when: A promoter requests reclassification as a public shareholder

rules.appliesToText: Listed entity where a promoter seeks reclassification as a public shareholder
rules.evidence: Promoter's request with its date of receipt; board minutes recording the views; application to each exchange; no-objection letter; shareholder resolution; notification to the exchanges
rules.notes: FOUR deadlines on the listed entity in one sequence, each running from a different event. The thirty days in Reg 31A(3)(a)(iv) is NOT one of them - it binds the recognised stock exchange to decide the application. The held compilation also prints two earlier versions of this provision in footnotes, carrying thirty days from shareholder approval and a three-to-six-month board-to-shareholders gap; both were replaced by the Third Amendment 2024 w.e.f. 13.12.2024 and neither is the law.

rules.title: Disclose a reclassification under a resolution plan within one day of the plan being approved
rules.detail: Where the reclassification of an existing promoter or promoter group is made under a resolution plan approved under section 31 of the Insolvency Code, the conditions in Reg 31A(5), (6) and (7)(b) do not apply, provided the existing promoter and promoter group do not remain in control and the reclassification, with the underlying rationale, is disclosed to the stock exchanges within one day of the resolution plan being approved.
rules.quote: such re-classification along with the underlying rationale shall be disclosed to the stock exchanges within one day of the resolution plan being approved
rules.frequency: On approval of a resolution plan
rules.timelineText: Within one day of the resolution plan being approved

due.when: Resolution plan approved under section 31 of the Insolvency Code

rules.appliesToText: Listed entity reclassifying a promoter under a resolution plan approved under section 31 of the Insolvency Code
rules.evidence: Tribunal order approving the resolution plan; disclosure to the exchanges with its filing timestamp
rules.notes: One day, not one working day - the regulation says day. This is the exemption route, and the disclosure is a CONDITION of it: miss the day and the ordinary Reg 31A(3) sequence applies instead.

rules.title: Re-approve any special right granted to shareholders by special resolution once every five years
rules.detail: Any special right granted to the shareholders of a listed entity is subject to approval by the shareholders in a general meeting by special resolution once in every five years, starting from the date the special right was granted. Special rights subsisting when the regulation came into force required approval by special resolution within five years of that date.
rules.quote: Any special right granted to the shareholders of a listed entity shall be subject to the approval by the shareholders in a general meeting by way of a special resolution once in every five years starting from the date of grant of such special right
rules.frequency: Once every five years per right granted
rules.timelineText: Once in every five years starting from the date of grant of the special right

due.when: Five years from the grant of the special right, and every five years after

rules.appliesToText: Listed entity that has granted any special right to a shareholder
rules.evidence: Instrument granting the special right with its date; special resolution re-approving it
rules.notes: A five-year clock that runs from the grant of each right, so different rights fall due on different dates. This app holds no register of special rights, so the cadence is stated and not computed. It is the kind of obligation that is met once and then forgotten for five years.

rules.title: Submit the Annual Information Memorandum to the stock exchanges
rules.detail: Submit an Annual Information Memorandum to the stock exchanges in the manner specified by the Board from time to time.
rules.quote: The listed entity shall submit to the stock exchange(s) an Annual Information Memorandum in the manner specified by the Board from time to time
rules.timelineText: In the manner specified by the Board from time to time
rules.appliesToText: Every listed entity
rules.evidence: Annual Information Memorandum as filed, with the exchange acknowledgement
rules.notes: The regulation delegates both the manner and the timing to the Board and fixes no period of its own. The obligation is real and its deadline is not in this text - which is a different thing from there being no deadline.

rules.title: File the draft scheme of arrangement with the stock exchanges and obtain a No-objection letter before approaching the Tribunal
rules.detail: File the draft scheme of arrangement, with the fee specified in Schedule XI, with the stock exchanges for a No-objection letter before filing the scheme with any Court or Tribunal; do not file the scheme with a Court or Tribunal until that letter is obtained; and place the letter before the Court or Tribunal when seeking approval. On sanction, submit the documents the Board or the exchanges prescribe.
rules.quote: the listed entity desirous of undertaking a scheme of arrangement or involved in a scheme of arrangement, shall file the draft scheme of arrangement, proposed to be filed before any Court or Tribunal under sections 391-394 and 101 of the Companies Act, 1956 or under Sections 230-234 and Section 66 of Companies Act, 2013, whichever applicable, along with a non-refundable fee as specified in Schedule XI, with the stock exchange(s) for obtaining the No-objection letter, before filing such scheme with any Court or Tribunal, in terms of requirements specified by the Board or stock exchange(s) from time to time. Provided that the validity of the No-objection letter of stock exchanges shall be six months from the date of issuance, within which the draft scheme of arrangement shall be submitted to the Court or Tribunal
rules.timelineText: Before filing the scheme with any Court or Tribunal; the No-objection letter is valid for six months from issue

due.when: Before filing a scheme of arrangement with a Court or Tribunal

rules.appliesToText: Listed entity undertaking or involved in a scheme of arrangement
rules.evidence: Draft scheme as filed with each exchange; fee receipt; No-objection letter with its date of issue; record of the letter being placed before the Tribunal
rules.notes: The six-month validity of the No-objection letter is a deadline of its own: the draft scheme must reach the Court or Tribunal inside it, or the letter lapses and the exchange process restarts.

rules.title: Obtain prior shareholder approval by special resolution before disposing of the whole or substantially the whole of an undertaking outside a scheme
rules.detail: Where a listed entity sells, leases or otherwise disposes of the whole or substantially the whole of its undertaking, or of any one of its undertakings, otherwise than under a scheme of arrangement, it must take prior approval of shareholders by special resolution and disclose the object, the commercial rationale and the use of the proceeds in the statement annexed to the notice. The special resolution is acted upon only if the votes cast by public shareholders in favour exceed those cast against.
rules.quote: A listed entity carrying out sale, lease or otherwise disposal of the whole or substantially the whole of the undertaking of such entity or where it owns more than one undertaking, of the whole or substantially the whole of any of such undertakings, shall - (a) take prior approval of shareholders by way of special resolution

due.when: Before a disposal of the whole or substantially the whole of an undertaking

rules.appliesToText: Listed entity disposing of the whole or substantially the whole of an undertaking outside a scheme of arrangement
rules.evidence: Notice with the annexed statement; special resolution; scrutiniser's report showing the public shareholder vote separately
rules.notes: The public-shareholder majority is a second and independent test: a special resolution can carry on the total vote and still fail this proviso. The scrutiniser's report therefore has to separate the public shareholders' votes, which an ordinary special resolution does not require.

rules.title: Observe the standing restrictions on lien, calls in advance and differential rights
rules.detail: Do not exercise a lien on fully paid shares, and on partly paid shares only for moneys called or payable at a fixed time; where an amount is paid in advance of calls, stipulate that it may carry interest but confers no right to dividend or to participate in profits; do not issue shares conferring superior or inferior rights as to dividend, or inferior voting rights, against equity shares already listed; and do not select listed securities for redemption otherwise than pro rata or by lot unless the terms of issue provide otherwise.
rules.quote: The listed entity shall not exercise a lien on its fully paid shares and that in respect of partly paid shares it shall not exercise any lien except in respect of moneys called or payable at a fixed time in respect of such shares
rules.appliesToText: Every listed entity
rules.evidence: Articles of association; terms of issue; register of members
rules.notes: Reg 41(9) and 41(10) - the annual certificate from a practising company secretary that share certificates were issued within thirty days of lodgement, and its filing with the exchanges - were OMITTED by the Third Amendment 2024 w.e.f. 13.12.2024. The held compilation still prints that wording, in a footnote, as the text prior to omission. It is not carried here as an obligation because it is no longer one. The proviso to Reg 41(3) permits a listed entity with SR equity shares to issue further SR equity shares to its SR shareholders through a bonus, split or rights issue.

rules.title: Intimate the record date to the stock exchanges at least three working days in advance
rules.detail: Intimate the record date to all stock exchanges where the entity is listed, or where derivatives on its stock are available or its stock forms part of an index on which derivatives are available, for a declaration of dividend, an issue of right or bonus shares, an issue of shares on conversion of debentures or other convertible securities, shares arising out of rights attached to such securities, corporate actions such as mergers, de-mergers and splits, and any other purpose the exchanges specify. Give notice of at least three working days, excluding the date of intimation and the record date; at least seven working days for corporate actions through a scheme of arrangement under Reg 37. Keep a gap of at least five working days between two record dates.
rules.quote: The listed entity shall give notice in advance of atleast three working days (excluding the date of intimation and the record date) to stock exchange(s) of record date specifying the purpose of the record date: Provided that in the case of corporate actions through schemes of arrangement covered under regulation 37, the listed entity shall give notice in advance of atleast seven working days (excluding the date of intimation and the record date). The listed entity shall ensure the time gap of at least five working days between two record dates
rules.timelineText: At least three working days in advance, excluding the date of intimation and the record date; at least seven working days for corporate actions through a scheme of arrangement under Reg 37; at least five working days between two record dates
rules.appliesToText: Every listed entity fixing a record date
rules.evidence: Intimation to each exchange with its filing timestamp; board or committee resolution fixing the record date
rules.notes: The two periods were SWAPPED by the Third Amendment 2024 w.e.f. 13.12.2024: the general notice went from seven working days to three, and the scheme-of-arrangement notice from three to seven. A Company Secretary working from memory will have them the wrong way round. The gap between two record dates changed in the same amendment from thirty days to five working days. Not computed - working days, both ends excluded, no exchange holiday calendar here, and the count runs backward from the record date so a calendar-day approximation would fall later than the regulation allows.

rules.title: Declare and disclose dividend on a per share basis only
rules.detail: Declare and disclose the dividend on a per share basis only.
rules.quote: The listed entity shall declare and disclose the dividend on per share basis only
rules.appliesToText: Every listed entity declaring a dividend
rules.evidence: Board resolution and the outcome filed with the exchanges, expressed per share
rules.notes: A manner requirement, not a filing: a dividend announced as a percentage of face value does not satisfy it. Reg 43(3) - recommending or declaring dividend at least five working days before the record date - and Reg 43(5) were OMITTED by the Third Amendment 2024 w.e.f. 13.12.2024, and the held text prints both only as the wording prior to omission.

rules.title: Satisfy the conditions for a change of name, and change the name within six months where the activities have changed
rules.detail: A change of name is permitted only where at least one year has elapsed since the last name change, and either at least fifty per cent of total revenue in the preceding one year came from the new activity suggested by the new name, or the amount invested in the new activity or project is at least fifty per cent of the assets. Where a listed entity has changed its activities and its name does not reflect them, it must change its name in line with those activities within six months of the change of activities.
rules.quote: if any listed entity has changed its activities which are not reflected in its name, it shall change its name in line with its activities within a period of six months from the change of activities in compliance of provisions as applicable to change of name prescribed under Companies Act, 2013
rules.frequency: On a change of name or of activities
rules.timelineText: Within a period of six months from the change of activities
rules.appliesToText: Listed entity that has changed its activities, or seeks to change its name
rules.evidence: Board and shareholder resolutions; revenue or investment computation supporting the fifty per cent test; certificate from a practising chartered accountant on compliance with the conditions
rules.notes: Two different obligations in one regulation: conditions that GATE a voluntary change of name, and a duty to change the name within six months where the activities have already moved. The second is the one nobody diarises. The application for the change must carry a certificate from a practising chartered accountant stating compliance with the Reg 45(1) conditions.

rules.title: No non-executive director aged seventy-five or more may be appointed or continue in office unless a special resolution is passed, with the justification in the explanatory statement
rules.detail: This is a continuing requirement, not a one-off. A director who crosses seventy-five in office must have a special resolution passed for the directorship to continue.
rules.quote: No listed entity shall appoint a person or continue the directorship of any person as a non -executive director who has attained the age of seventy five years unless a special resolution is passed to that effect
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed. Reg 15(2) exemption: these corporate governance provisions do not apply where paid-up equity share capital does not exceed Rs 10 crore AND net worth does not exceed Rs 25 crore on the last day of the previous financial year.

rules.title: Fill any vacancy in the office of a director at the earliest and in any case within three months of the vacancy
rules.detail: The period runs from the date the vacancy arises, which this app does not record - there is no register of board vacancies here, so no date is computed. Where the vacancy causes non-compliance with Reg 18(1), 19(1) or (2), 20(2) or (2A), or 21(2) or (3), the proviso requires compliance at the earliest and in any case within three months.
rules.quote: Any vacancy in the office of a director shall be filled by th e listed entity at the earliest and in any case not later than three months from the date
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed. Reg 15(2) exemption: these corporate governance provisions do not apply where paid-up equity share capital does not exceed Rs 10 crore AND net worth does not exceed Rs 25 crore on the last day of the previous financial year.
rules.timelineText: Within three months of the vacancy

due.when: A vacancy arises in the office of a director

rules.title: Board meeting quorum: one-third of total strength or three directors, whichever is higher, including at least one independent director
rules.detail: A board meeting held without an independent director present is inquorate for a top 2000 entity however many directors attend.
rules.quote: The quorum for every meeting of the board of directors of the top 2000 listed entities shall be one -third of its total strength or three directors, whichever is higher, including at least one independent director
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed, top 2000 by market capitalisation. This app does not hold a market capitalisation rank, so that test cannot be evaluated here - confirm it before relying on this row. Equity-listed. Reg 15(2) exemption: these corporate governance provisions do not apply where paid-up equity share capital does not exceed Rs 10 crore AND net worth does not exceed Rs 25 crore on the last day of the previous financial year.

rules.title: Board to satisfy itself that plans are in place for orderly succession to the board and to senior management
rules.detail: Evidenced by the minute recording that the board considered succession. Nothing is filed.
rules.quote: The board of directors of the listed entity shall satisfy itself that pla ns are in place for orderly succession for appointment to the board of directors and senior management
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed. Reg 15(2) exemption: these corporate governance provisions do not apply where paid-up equity share capital does not exceed Rs 10 crore AND net worth does not exceed Rs 25 crore on the last day of the previous financial year.

rules.title: Place the minimum information specified in Part A of Schedule II before the board of directors
rules.detail: Part A of Schedule II lists the items - annual operating plans, quarterly results, minutes of committee meetings, default information, and others. The Schedule is in the held compilation; the individual items are not carried as separate rules here.
rules.quote: The minimum information to be placed before the board of directors is specified in Part A of Schedule II
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed. Reg 15(2) exemption: these corporate governance provisions do not apply where paid-up equity share capital does not exceed Rs 10 crore AND net worth does not exceed Rs 25 crore on the last day of the previous financial year.

rules.title: Constitute a qualified and independent audit committee: minimum three directors, at least two-thirds independent, all financially literate and at least one with accounting or related financial management expertise
rules.detail: The register carried the audit committee MEETING requirement (Reg 18(2)(a)) without the requirement to constitute the committee at all. Note the composition test is stricter than s.177 of the Companies Act, which requires only a majority of independent directors - a listed entity must meet this one. Where the entity has outstanding SR equity shares the committee must comprise only independent directors.
rules.quote: Every listed entity shall constitute a qualified and independent audit committee in accordance with the terms of reference, subject to the following: (a) The audit committee shall have minimum three directors as members.

rules.title: The role of the audit committee and the information it must review are as specified in Part C of Schedule II
rules.detail: Part C of Schedule II sets the terms of reference. The Schedule is in the held compilation; its individual items are not carried as separate rules here.
rules.quote: The role of the audit committee and the information to be reviewed by the audit committee shall be as specified in Part C of Schedule II
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed. Reg 15(2) exemption: these corporate governance provisions do not apply where paid-up equity share capital does not exceed Rs 10 crore AND net worth does not exceed Rs 25 crore on the last day of the previous financial year.

rules.title: Constitute the nomination and remuneration committee: at least three directors, all non-executive, and at least two-thirds independent

rules.quote: The board of directors shall constitute the nomination and remuneration committee as follows: (a) the committee shall comprise of at least three directors ; (b) all directors of the committee shall be non -executive directors; and (c) at least two-thirds of the directors shall be independent directors

rules.title: The chairperson of the nomination and remuneration committee shall be an independent director
rules.detail: Distinct from the composition test in Reg 19(1): a committee can be two-thirds independent and still be chaired by the wrong person.
rules.quote: The Chairperson of the nomination and remuneration committee shall be an independent director
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed. Reg 15(2) exemption: these corporate governance provisions do not apply where paid-up equity share capital does not exceed Rs 10 crore AND net worth does not exceed Rs 25 crore on the last day of the previous financial year.

rules.title: Quorum for a nomination and remuneration committee meeting: two members or one third of the committee, whichever is greater, including at least one independent director in attendance
rules.detail: Note "whichever is GREATER" here, against "whichever is HIGHER" for the Risk Management Committee in Reg 21(3B) - the same test, worded differently in the two regulations.
rules.quote: The quorum for a meeting of the nomination and remuneration committee shall be either two members or one third of the members of the committee, whichever is greater, including at least one independent director in attendance
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed. Reg 15(2) exemption: these corporate governance provisions do not apply where paid-up equity share capital does not exceed Rs 10 crore AND net worth does not exceed Rs 25 crore on the last day of the previous financial year.

rules.title: The role of the nomination and remuneration committee is as specified in Part D of Schedule II

rules.title: At least three directors, with at least one independent director, shall be members of the Stakeholders Relationship Committee

rules.title: The role of the Stakeholders Relationship Committee is as specified in Part D of Schedule II

rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed. Reg 15(2) exemption: these corporate governance provisions do not apply where paid-up equity share capital does not exceed Rs 10 crore AND net worth does not exceed Rs 25 crore on the last day of the previous financial year.

rules.title: Constitute a Risk Management Committee

rules.title: Do not register a transfer where a statutory prohibition, attachment or prohibitory order of a competent authority restrains it
rules.detail: A refusal that is required, not permitted. Registering in the face of an order is the breach.
rules.quote: The listed entity shall not register transfer when any statutory prohibition or any attachment or prohibitory order of a competent authority restrains it from transferring the securities from the na me of the transferor(s).
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed

rules.title: Do not register a transfer where the transferor objects, subject to the condition in the proviso
rules.detail: The sixty working days in the proviso bind the TRANSFEROR, who must serve a prohibitory order within that time. Reading it as the entity deadline would put a duty on the company that Reg 40(5) does not impose.
rules.quote: The listed entity shall not register the transfer of its securities in the name of the transferee(s) when the transferor(s) objects to the transfer: Provided that the transferor serves on the listed entity, within sixty working days of raising the objection, a prohibitory order of a Court of competent jurisdiction.
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed

rules.title: Comply with all procedural requirements for transfer and transmission of securities as specified by the Board from time to time
rules.detail: A delegating provision: the requirements live in SEBI circulars, which are not held here.
rules.quote: 414[The listed entity shall comply with all procedural requirements with respect to transfer and transmission of securities as specified by the Board from time to time.
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed

rules.title: The dividend distribution policy must contain the parameters Reg 43(2) lists
rules.detail: Circumstances in which shareholders may or may not expect dividend, the financial parameters, internal and external factors, the policy on retained earnings and on utilisation of retained earnings. A policy missing any of them does not meet Reg 43(2).
rules.quote: The dividend distribution policy shall include the following parameters: (a) the circumstances under which the shareholders of the listed entities may or may not expect dividend; (b) the financial parameters that shall be considered while declaring dividend; (c) internal and external factors that shall be considered for declaration of dividend; (d) policy as to how the retained earnings shall be utilized;
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed

rules.title: Provide remote e-voting to shareholders in respect of ALL shareholder resolutions
rules.detail: All resolutions, without exception. The register carried the Reg 44(3) results-submission duty and never the duty to provide the facility at all.
rules.quote: The listed entity shall provide the facility of remote e-voting facility to its shareholders, in respect of all shareholders' resolutions .
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed

rules.title: Provide the e-voting facility in compliance with the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules 2014
rules.detail: Those Rules are not held in reference/, so their requirements rest on the Act side rather than on a text held here.
rules.quote: The e -voting facility to be provided to shareholders in terms of sub -regulation (1), shall be provided in compliance with the conditions specified under the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014 , or amendments made thereto .
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed

rules.title: Send proxy forms to holders of securities, stating that a holder may vote either for or against each resolution
rules.detail: The proviso disapplies this for a general meeting held only through electronic means.
rules.quote: The listed entity shall send proxy forms to holders of securities in all cases mentioning that a holder may vote either for or against each resolution 437[:] 438[Provided that the requirement to send proxy forms shall not be applicable to general meetings held only through electronic mode .]
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed

rules.title: Maintain a functional website containing the basic information about the listed entity
rules.detail: Functional is the operative word. The contents required are in Reg 46(2), which the register already carries.
rules.quote: The listed entity shall maintain a functional website containing the basic information about the listed entity.
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed

rules.title: Publish the Reg 47(1) information in at least one English national daily circulating in substantially the whole of India AND one daily in the language of the region of the registered office
rules.detail: Two publications, not one. The register carried the Reg 47(1) duty to publish and not the requirement about where.
rules.quote: The information at sub -regulation (1) shall be published in at least one English language national daily newspaper circulating in the whole or substantially the whole of India and in one daily newspaper published in the language of the region, where the registered office of the listed entity is situated:
rules.appliesToText: Equity-listed
